prompt: Return the first non-empty Optional of three, using Optional.or chaining rather than isPresent checks.
explanation: Optional.or takes a Supplier of another Optional and only invokes it when the receiver is empty, so a.or(() -> b).or(() -> c) short-circuits at the first present value. This expresses 'first non-empty of several' declaratively, without an isPresent/get ladder, and naturally yields empty when every option is empty.
hints: Optional has an or method (since Java 9) that takes a Supplier<Optional<T>> used only when the receiver is empty.
Chain twice: a.or(() -> b).or(() -> c). If all three are empty, the chain result is simply empty.
